business_problem: Banks struggled to identify authorized push payment scams in real time, because customers themselves authorized transfers and criminals moved stolen funds through mule accounts.
solution_summary: Mastercard’s Consumer Fraud Risk is live in the U.K. and uses Mastercard’s account-to-account payment network view together with large-scale payment data and insights from five years of bank-supported tracing of funds through suspected mule accounts. The solution analyzes factors including account names, payment values, payer and payee history, and links between a payee and accounts associated with scams. Mastercard’s AI uses this evidence to identify and predict scam payments, providing intelligence and a score that participating banks can combine with their own customer and behavioral insights to target fraud strategies and intervene before funds leave a victim’s account. TSB was an early adopter and used the tool in its fraud-prevention work. The release does not identify storage systems, model type, or a technical interface, so those architecture details cannot be specified.

solution_components.name: Consumer Fraud Risk
solution_components.role: Analyzes payment and scam-account signals to provide banks with intelligence for identifying and stopping suspected scam payments.

data_flow: Account-to-account payment data and traced links among suspected mule accounts are assessed using account names, payment values, payer and payee history, and payee links to scam-associated accounts. Consumer Fraud Risk provides scam-risk intelligence and a score to participating banks, which can combine it with customer and behavioral insights to intervene before funds leave the payer’s account.
integration_points: U.K. banks’ real-time account-to-account payment systems
business_outcome: TSB reported dramatically increased fraud detection after using the solution for four months. Based on TSB’s results, the release estimated that annual scam payments prevented could equate to almost £100 million saved across the U.K. if all banks matched its performance.
metrics: almost £100m saved across the U.K. should its performance be mirrored by all banks
£97 million would be saved across the banking sector based on latest UKF data
architecture_clues: Consumer Fraud Risk was live in the U.K.; further international markets were being assessed for rollout.
Mastercard had worked with U.K. banks for five years to trace funds through mule accounts.

source_references.title: Mastercard leverages its AI capabilities to fight real-time payment scams

evidence_quotes: Based on insights from this tracing activity and overlaying them with specific analysis factors such as account names, payment values, payer and payee history, and the payee’s links to accounts associated with scams, Mastercard’s AI solution provides banks with the intelligence necessary to intervene in real time and stop a payment before funds are lost.
TSB is one of the first banks to adopt Mastercard’s Consumer Fraud Risk tool and is already using it to great effect.
In just four months, the bank says it has dramatically increased its fraud detection.
£97 million would be saved across the banking sector based on latest UKF data.
